stem: A media company has 30 accounts in AWS Organizations. A compliance scanner that runs in the central security account must read resource configurations in every member account, and human auditors must sign in once with the corporate identity provider and get read-only access to all accounts. Which TWO actions meet these requirements? (Select TWO.)

choices.text: In each member account, create a read-only role whose trust policy names the scanner's role, and have the scanner call sts:AssumeRole
Create an IAM user with access keys in each member account and store the 30 key pairs in the scanner's configuration
Attach an SCP to the organization root that grants the security account read access to resources in all member accounts
Connect IAM Identity Center to the corporate IdP and assign the auditors group a read-only permission set on all accounts
Create an IAM group with the ReadOnlyAccess managed policy in the management account and add each auditor's IAM user to it

rationale: A read-only role in each member account that trusts the scanner's role lets the scanner call sts:AssumeRole and work with temporary credentials, which is the IAM pattern for cross-account delegation. IAM Identity Center connected to the corporate IdP gives auditors one sign-in, and assigning a permission set makes Identity Center create matching roles in each target account. IAM users with access keys in every account create 30 sets of long-term credentials, which IAM best practices tell you to avoid for workloads. An SCP never grants permissions; it only sets the maximum permissions available. An IAM group in the management account grants permissions only in that account and cannot give its users access to resources in member accounts.
